title: Cords of Love
backstory: Israel kept drifting, and Hosea kept speaking. God's words through the prophets came down hard, and his judgments went out like light (Hosea 6:5). Yet in the same book he speaks as a father remembering a small child — taking Ephraim by the arms, teaching him to walk, lifting the heavy yoke off him and laying food in front of him (Hosea 11:3-4). Israel had eaten its fill and forgotten him (Hosea 13:6), but God had not forgotten Israel.

passages.synopsis: Hosea gave Israel the words of a homecoming song. Come, let us return unto the LORD, for the one who has torn is the one who will heal. He will revive us and raise us up to live in his sight. If we follow on to know the LORD, he will come to us as surely as the morning and the rain.

God answered with a father's ache. Israel's goodness was like a morning cloud and the early dew — lovely for a moment, then gone. So God had sent his prophets with words that cut like a sword, and his judgment went out as plain as the morning light. What he wanted was not more burnt offerings but mercy, and hearts that truly knew him.

God remembered Israel's beginning like a parent remembering a toddler. When Israel was a child he loved him and called his son out of Egypt. He taught Ephraim to walk, took them by the arms, and healed them, though they never knew it. He drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love, and bent down to feed them.

But the child had grown and turned away, bent on backsliding. Trouble was coming through Assyria, and it broke God's heart. How shall I give thee up, Ephraim, God cried — for I am God, and not man. In the end his children would come trembling home like doves, and he would settle them in their houses.

scrambleVerses.text: When Israel was a child, then I loved him,
Come, and let us return unto the LORD:
For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice;

triviaQuestions.question: According to Hosea, what did God desire more than sacrifice?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Hosea 6:6 — "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings."

triviaQuestions.question: Out of what land did God call his son?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 — "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt."

triviaQuestions.question: With what did God say he drew his people?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Hosea 11:4 — "I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love: and I was to them as they that take off the yoke on their jaws, and I laid meat unto them."

triviaQuestions.question: Why did God say he would not destroy Ephraim in his anger?
options: Because he is God, and not man
triviaQuestions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 — "I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee: and I will not enter into the city."

reflection: God remembered teaching Israel to walk and drawing them with bands of love. When have you felt God gently drawing you back to himself?
